74f8a1f186:
Participants will acquire the skills needed for assessment and treatment using cognitive behavioral therapy according to the three-phase model.

## First year - simple trauma

The course will focus on treating simple trauma - trauma caused by exposure to a single event in adulthood. During the first year, we teach trauma assessment tools, structuring treatment and case conceptualization according to CBT principles, and the three-phase model of trauma treatment, including emotion regulation, various exposure techniques and cognitive interventions.

## Second year - treating complex trauma

Complex post-traumatic stress disorder is caused by exposure to multiple or prolonged traumatic events, such as captivity, prolonged combat, domestic violence, abuse or neglect in childhood.

Therapists frequently encounter symptoms such as difficulty trusting, a tendency toward self-destructiveness, alexithymia (difficulty putting feelings into words), chronic depression, symptoms associated with borderline personality disorder, or dissociative symptoms. Many of these symptoms can be attributed to complex trauma, and they are often resistant to conventional treatment.

Pierre Janet developed the three-phase model for treating such disorders in the 19th century. His model has since been adapted and developed by modern clinicians (e.g., van der Hart). Many people coping with complex trauma suffer from a wide range of co-occurring disorders, such as substance abuse, poor social skills and anxiety disorders, which must be treated before the trauma itself can be addressed. This makes treating complex trauma longer and more complicated than usual. This training teaches methods for treating severe personality disorders.

During the second year, we focus on complex trauma, which in many cases is accompanied by anxiety disorders, depression, complex personality disorders such as borderline personality disorder, dissociative disorders, difficulties with impulse control, and difficulty functioning independently. The second year provides a theoretical framework for understanding these disorders in the context of trauma and in other contexts, along with practical training in therapeutic tools such as mindfulness, DBT, schema therapy and ACT.

## Program details

Our training course combines methods from classic cognitive behavioral therapy (exposure methods, e.g., Foa and others; cognitive therapy, e.g., Clark, Ehlers and others), integrating them into the three-phase model of trauma treatment (Janet, van der Hart). This model sequences the interventions so that the client is not flooded by painful memories before learning to regulate their level of arousal. Our training emphasizes mind-body approaches and includes third-wave CBT models such as mindfulness, DBT and acceptance and commitment therapy.

Teaching methods include lectures, reading and discussing academic papers, live demonstrations and films, practicing the techniques taught, and clinical supervision on cases. The treatment methods taught are used in treating trauma as well as anxiety disorders, dissociative disorders, depression and other disorders.

fba994c20e:
At Metiv, the center for the treatment of psychological trauma, we have been treating, researching and teaching trauma therapy for 30 years. Over these years, the understanding of psychological trauma and its treatment has changed, and recent years in Israel have challenged these approaches even further as we encounter many manifestations of trauma's effects. There are many protocols for treating trauma, but the expected magic often does not happen in the clinic.

In our work with trauma survivors, we see that a deep and broad understanding of trauma's effects on the brain and body is needed, along with its thoughtful and flexible application. Trauma therapy often creates helplessness and situations of being stuck, and the tools we are used to are not enough to bring about change.

The Roadmap for Trauma Therapy course:

- Was built from our long and varied experience, and lays out guidelines, compasses and a toolbox that together help therapists find their way through the tangle of trauma and make decisions that move treatment forward - what is right to do and when - and also addresses the therapist's own therapeutic stance at every stage of treatment.
- Lays a stable, deep foundation that gives an understanding of direction and path, of the phases, and of working with different trauma presentations.
- Includes theoretical knowledge and extensive clinical experience, as well as exercises that ground the understanding in practice.

The course is practical, not only theoretical, and allows therapists to understand in depth, acquire skills, grow more confident in their work, and develop the ability to work in varied ways within the complex field of trauma.

After the course, you can join a 5-session supervision group in which participants can bring cases from their practice for consultation and work planning, and learn from other participants' cases. Additional fee; subject to the number of participants.
